task: Your manager Tom stops by for a quick check-in. Give a short update on your current project and answer his follow-ups. Lead with where things stand.
zh: 经理 Tom 路过你的工位，想快速了解一下进度。简短汇报你手上项目的情况，并回答他的追问。先说项目目前进展到哪一步。
role: Tom, the learner's manager at an IT services company. Friendly but busy; wants dates, risks and whether he needs to do anything.
setting: Quick check-in at the learner's desk. If the learner is vague, ask for a date or a number. If they mention a problem, ask what they need from you.
say: Morning! Just doing the rounds. How's your project tracking this week?

words.en: one thing I need from you

task: In your weekly 1:1, your manager Sarah asks why the go-live date of your project has slipped by two weeks. Explain the reason (a real one from your work, or make one up), the new date, and what you're doing so it doesn't slip again.
zh: 每周一对一面谈时，经理 Sarah 问你为什么项目上线日期推迟了两周。说明原因（可以用工作中的真实原因，也可以编一个）、新的日期，以及你打算怎么避免再次延期。
role: Sarah, the learner's manager. Calm and supportive, but she has to explain the delay to the client and her own boss, so she wants a clear reason and a date she can trust.
setting: A private 1:1 in a small meeting room. The go-live has moved by two weeks. Ask why it happened, how confident the learner is in the new date, what could make it slip again, and whether anyone saw it coming. If the answer is fuzzy, ask for a specific date.
say: So, I saw the go-live's moved out by two weeks. Talk me through what happened?

task: The client's project manager Mike calls you for a progress update. Tell him where the project is, what's done, what's next and anything he needs to know.
zh: 客户的项目经理 Mike 打电话来问进度。告诉他项目现在的进展、已完成的部分、下一步计划，以及他需要知道的事情。
role: Mike, the project manager on the client side. Detail-oriented and polite; he reports to his own boss every Friday, so he wants percentages, dates and anything that needs his action.
setting: A short Teams call. Ask follow-ups about whatever the learner mentions: how far along it is, when the next milestone is, whether anything is waiting on the client side. If the learner uses jargon, ask what it means for his users.
say: Hi, thanks for jumping on. So, where are we at with everything?

words.en: what it means for your users
words.zh: 这对你们的用户意味着什么

words.en: the one thing to be aware of

task: You're at the client's monthly steering group meeting. Helen, a member of the group, asks you about the budget and the main risks on your project. Answer clearly and honestly.
zh: 你在参加客户每月一次的项目指导委员会会议。委员会成员 Helen 问你项目的预算情况和主要风险。清楚、诚实地回答。
role: Helen, the client's finance director and a steering group member. Sharp and a bit sceptical; she cares about money, surprises and who is responsible for each risk.
setting: A formal steering group meeting. Ask whether the project is on budget, what the biggest risk is, how likely it is, what it would cost if it happened and what the plan is. If the learner says everything is fine, politely challenge that.
say: Before we move on, I'd like to hear about budget and risks. Are we still on track financially?

task: Raj has just joined as your new manager. He asks you for an overview of the project you're working on. Explain the big picture, then answer his questions.
zh: Raj 刚加入，成为你的新经理。他请你介绍一下你在做的项目。先讲整体情况，再回答他的问题。
role: Raj, the learner's new manager, in his first week at the company. Curious, friendly and asks lots of basic questions because he's learning everything at once.
setting: A get-to-know-you chat over coffee. Ask about the client, the goal, the team, the timeline and what the learner's own role is. Ask what he should keep an eye on.
say: Thanks for making time. I'm still finding my feet, so give me the big picture of your project?

task: Aroha from the network team messages and then calls you. Her team has work that your project depends on, or that depends on you. Explain what you need from her team, by when, and what happens if it's late.
zh: 网络组的 Aroha 先发消息然后打电话给你。你的项目和她们组的工作互相依赖。说明你需要她们组做什么、什么时候之前要完成，以及如果晚了会有什么影响。
role: Aroha, the team lead of the network team at the same company. Practical and organised; her team is juggling several projects, so she wants exact requirements and real deadlines, not 'as soon as possible'.
setting: A quick call to plan work between two teams. Ask exactly what the learner needs, the hard deadline, whether anything can wait, and what the learner's team will deliver to hers. If a deadline sounds soft, ask what really happens if it's missed.
say: Kia ora, I'm trying to plan my team's next few weeks. What do you need from us, and when?

task: It's Friday afternoon. Your team lead Priya asks how your week went. Sum up what you got done, what's still open, and your plan for next week.
zh: 周五下午，组长 Priya 问你这周过得怎么样。总结一下这周完成了什么、还有什么没做完，以及下周的计划。
role: Priya, the learner's team lead. Relaxed and encouraging on a Friday; she likes to hear about wins and wants to know if anything will be a problem on Monday.
setting: End-of-week wrap-up chat in the office kitchen. Ask what went well, what didn't get finished and why, and what the first thing on Monday is. Celebrate wins briefly.
say: Hey, nearly the weekend! How did your week go? Get through everything you wanted to?
